newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures firmer, seen holding steady.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures firmer, seen holding steady.

text.p: IPE oil futures opened slightly stronger than expected and held firm in light early trade on Wednesday, brokers said.
"Things are pretty quiet, but I think we could see the market move up a bit more," a broker said.
January Brent was trading up 17 cents at $22.91 a barrel at 1055 GMT, while December gas oil was up 75 cents at $217.75 a tonne.
Both Brent and gas oil tested resistance levels, with Brent breaching $22.95 and gas oil $218.00, but soon retreated, brokers said.
Cold weather expected over the Thanksgiving holiday weekend in the U.S. and the latest American Petroleum Institute (API) figures were supporting prices, brokers said.
The API showed overall distillate stocks rising 660,000 barrels to 118.2 million, but East Coast heating stocks fell over one million barrels to 30.2 million.
Crude stocks fell 2.0 million barrels to 300.3 million.
"On the whole, the figures were mildly bullish," a broker said.
The belief that any Iraqi oil sales could be absorbed into the market without upsetting prices also buoyed prices, brokers said.

OPEC's biannual conference begins on Wednesday in Vienna with ministers expected to agree to a rollover into 1997 of current production quotas. The first plenary session is scheduled for 1400 GMT. The meeting is unlikely to end today, OPEC Secretary-General Rilwanu Lukman told reporters in Vienna.
Ministers were said to trust that strong consumer demand for winter fuel would mop up any oil sales by Iraq and keep prices firm.
